newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: South African c/a deficit 3.5 bln rand in 3Q - Bank.
newsitem.headline: South African c/a deficit 3.5 bln rand in 3Q - Bank.

text.p: South Africa's current account deficit shrank to 3.5 billion rand in the third quarter from a revised 4.7 billion rand in the second quarter, the Reserve Bank said in its quarterly bulletin released on Thursday.
It said this brought the cumulative deficit to 10.5 billion rand for the year so far.
As a ratio of gross domestic product, the current account deficit fell to 2.0 percent from 3.1 percent in the second quarter.

The bank said the main reason for the improvement on the current account was a sharp increase in the value of merchandise exports, which was in part helped by the rand's depreciation this year, and net gold exports.
The rand has lost almost 30 percent of its value against the U.S. dollar this year.

The bank said the value of merchandise exports rose to a seasonally adjusted and annualised 102.8 billion rand in the third quarter from 94.3 billion rand in the second quarter, while volumes rose by just more than seven percent.
The value of net gold exports rose to 26.5 billion rand from 20.8 billion rand in the second quarter.
On the capital account, negative investor perceptions of South Africa resulted in a 0.2 billion rand net outflow compared with an inflow of 1.4 billion rand in the first two quarters of the year.
The outflow included various payment commitments in terms of existing agreements for the repayment of foreign debt previously affected by debt standstill arrangements.
Long-term capital expenditure reversed to a net outflow of of 0.1 billion rand from an inflow of 1.9 billion rand in the second quarter and 4.3 billion in the first.
Short-term capital to the tune of a net 0.1 billion rand also left the country in the third quarter compared with a net inflow of 0.7 billion rand in the second quarter.
